technical_and_design_decisions: Implement new API functions for adding/removing/updating consortiums, orderer configurations, and MSP fields using a fluent interface pattern consistent with existing fabric-config APIs.
Use protobuf-based config structures from Hyperledger Fabric for all configuration manipulations.
For U2, return a ConfigUpdateEnvelope without signing identities by leveraging unsigned envelope generation.
For U3 and U4, implement removal functions that directly manipulate the ConfigGroup structure to delete specific fields.
For U5, implement add/remove consenter functions that match all four fields (host, port, client cert, server cert) for safe removal.
For U6, build a CLI tool using Go that parses JSON input, interacts with peers via gRPC, and supports dry-run mode.
For U7 and U8, add individual setter methods for each configurable field while preserving existing Get/Set patterns.
Use existing testing frameworks (Go test) for unit and integration tests.
Follow Hyperledger Fabric coding standards and contribution guidelines.
assumptions: The development environment is already set up with Go, Hyperledger Fabric dependencies, and necessary tools.
Existing fabric-config library codebase is accessible and understood by the developer.
Unit tests are sufficient for validation; no extensive end-to-end testing with a live Fabric network is required.
Documentation updates are included within the scope of each user story.
Example code updates are part of the implementation for each feature.
The developer has prior experience with Hyperledger Fabric internals and Go programming.
No external dependencies beyond the standard Hyperledger Fabric libraries are needed.
Code reviews and CI/CD pipeline integration are handled separately and not part of this effort estimate.
